blocks.tk: Garagum kanaly Türkmenistanyň iň uly suw ýoly. Ol Amyderýadan başlanýar we günbatara, Garagum çölüniň günorta gyrasy boýunça uzap gidýär. Onuň uzynlygy Britannikanyň maglumatyna görä 1400 kilometr töweregi, Wikipediýanyň maglumatyna görä bolsa 1375 kilometr.
blocks.en: The Karakum Canal is Turkmenistan's largest waterway. It leaves the Amu Darya soon after the river enters the country and runs west along the southern edge of the Karakum desert, past Mary, Tejen and Ashgabat, towards the Caspian. Britannica gives its length as about 1,400 km, Wikipedia as 1,375 km; either way it is one of the longest irrigation canals in the world.

blocks.tk: Kanal 1954-nji ýylda gazylyp başlandy. Amyderýanyň suwy oňa 1956-njy ýylda goýberildi. Kanalyň esasy bölegi, Amyderýadan Gökdepä çenli 840 kilometrlik bölegi, 1967-nji ýylda gutaryldy. 1970–1980-nji ýyllarda täze bölekler gazyldy we kanal Hazar deňziniň kenaryna golaýlady. Kanalyň boýunda suw howdanlary hem guruldy: olar gyşky suwy tomus üçin saklaýar, olaryň iň ulusy Hanhowuz. Kanalyň 450 kilometrinde gämi ýörüp bilýär.
blocks.en: Digging began in 1954, after an earlier and more northerly scheme, the Main Turkmen Canal, had been abandoned. Amu Darya water first flowed into the new canal in 1956. The main section, about 840 km from the river to Gökdepe, west of Ashgabat, was finished in 1967; in the 1970s and 1980s further sections took it towards the Caspian coast. Reservoirs were built along it, the largest at Hanhowuz, to store winter water for the summer, and about 450 km of the canal is navigable.

blocks.tk: Kanal çöle suw getirdi. Onuň boýunda täze ekin meýdanlary döredildi, Murgabyň we Tejeniň köne oazisleri has köp suw aldy. FAO-nyň maglumatyna görä, Türkmenistanda suwarylýan ýerler 1975-nji ýylda 857 müň gektar bolan bolsa, 1994-nji ýylda 1,7 million gektardan geçdi. Bu ýerlerde esasan pagta we bugdaý ekilýär. Kanal Aşgabady hem suw bilen üpjün edýär.
blocks.en: The canal brought water to the desert. New fields were laid out along it, and the old oases of the Murgap and the Tejen received more water. According to FAO, Turkmenistan's irrigated land grew from about 857,000 hectares in 1975 to some 1.74 million in 1994, most of it sown with cotton and wheat. The canal also carries water to Ashgabat; Wikipedia puts its flow at about 13 cubic kilometres a year.

blocks.tk: Ýöne bu suw bir ýerden gelýär. Amyderýa ozal Aral deňzine guýýardy. 1960-njy ýyllarda Amyderýanyň we Syrderýanyň suwuny ekin meýdanlary üçin has köp alyp başladylar we Aral deňzi kiçelip başlady. Amerikan geografy Filip Miklin 1988-nji ýylda şeýle ýazdy: Garagum kanaly Arala gelýän suwuň azalmagynyň iň esasy sebäbi bolupdyr. 1956–1986-njy ýyllarda kanala 225 kub kilometr suw gidipdir, bu suwuň hiç bir damjasy Arala ýetmändir.
blocks.en: But that water comes from somewhere. The Amu Darya used to flow into the Aral Sea. From the 1960s ever more of its water, and of the Syr Darya's, was taken to irrigate the desert, and the sea began to shrink. In 1988 the American geographer Philip Micklin called the Karakum Canal “the single most important factor” in the falling inflow to the Aral: between 1956 and 1986 some 225 cubic kilometres went into it, the yearly amount rising from under 1 to more than 14, and none of that water reached the sea.

blocks.tk: Kanalyň köp ýeri ýönekeý topraga gazylan. Şonuň üçin suwuň bir bölegi ýere siňýär ýa-da bugarýar. FAO-nyň 1990-njy ýyllardaky hasabyna görä, akymyň 18 göterimi ýitýär; NASA-nyň ýazmagyna görä bolsa, toprak kanallarda suwuň takmynan ýarysy meýdanlara ýetmeýär. Siňen suw ýerasty suwuň derejesini galdyrýar, ýerler batgalaşýar we şorlaşýar. 1994-nji ýylda suwarylýan ýerleriň 37 göterimi şor ýer hasaplanýardy.
blocks.en: Much of the canal is dug into bare earth, without a lining, so part of its water soaks into the ground or evaporates. Estimates of the loss differ: FAO put it at about 18% of the flow in the 1990s and linked the canal's unprotected banks to waterlogging and salt in the land around it, while NASA's Earth Observatory writes that the earthen channels lose nearly half of their water before it reaches the fields. The seeping water raises the water table and brings salt to the surface; in 1994, FAO counted about 37% of Turkmenistan's irrigated land as saline.

blocks.tk: Häzir Aral deňzi öňküsiniň kiçijik bir bölegi. NASA-nyň maglumatyna görä, onuň guran düýbünden turýan duzly tozan töweregindäki meýdanlara we adamlaryň saglygyna zyýan ýetirýär. Garagum kanaly bolsa Türkmenistan üçin häzir hem esasy suw çeşmesi: onuň suwy bilen meýdanlar suwarylýar, şäherlere suw berilýär. Kanalyň hem peýdasy, hem zyýany bar.
blocks.en: Today the Aral Sea is a small fraction of its 1960 size. NASA describes how salty dust, laced with farm chemicals, blows off its dry bed onto the fields around it and has become a hazard to public health. The Karakum Canal, meanwhile, is still Turkmenistan's main source of water: it irrigates the fields and supplies the towns. It has brought both benefit and harm.

blocks.title: Reading the Turkmen
blocks.text: The passive is everywhere in this text: *gazylyp başlandy*, *goýberildi*, *gutaryldy*, *döredildi*, *ekilýär*, *suwarylýar*. Notice how rarely it says who did the work: that is what the passive is for. In the third paragraph, *bolan bolsa* is the **while, whereas** of *bolsa* ([B1 unit 9](b1-u09)): 857,000 hectares then, against 1.7 million later.

vocab.en: to flow into (of a river); to pour

questions.q: When did Amu Darya water first flow into the canal?
questions.explain: *Amyderýanyň suwy oňa 1956-njy ýylda goýberildi.* Digging began in 1954; the main section was finished in 1967.

questions.q: What did Philip Micklin conclude in 1988?
options: the canal was the biggest single cause of the falling inflow to the Aral
the canal had refilled the Aral Sea
the canal had no effect on the Aral Sea

options: it raises the water table and brings salt to the surface
it flows back into the Amu Darya

sources.title: Karakum Canal
sources.note: Turkmen Garagum Kanaly; main section begun 1954 and completed 1967, about 840 km from the Amu Darya to Gökdepe; extended to the Caspian coast in the 1970s and 1980s, about 1,400 km in all; navigable for 450 km

sources.title: Karakum Canal
sources.note: 1,375 km; about 13 km³ of water a year; supplies Ashgabat; opened large areas to cotton; Hanhowuz reservoir; a major factor in the Aral Sea disaster

sources.title: Main Turkmen Canal
sources.note: The earlier, more northerly scheme, abandoned in the 1950s; construction of the Karakum Canal began in 1954 along a route far to the south

sources.title: Desiccation of the Aral Sea: A Water Management Disaster in the Soviet Union
sources.note: The Karakum Canal “the single most important factor” in the reduced inflow to the Aral; 1,300 km; 225 km³ diverted between 1956 and 1986, the yearly withdrawal rising from under 1 to more than 14 km³; all of it lost to the Aral

sources.title: Irrigation in the countries of the former Soviet Union in figures: Turkmenistan
sources.note: About 1,300 km, capacity 630 m³/s, water to Ashgabat and the southern oases; losses estimated at 18% of the flow; unprotected banks and the waterlogging and salinization of nearby land; Hauz-Khan (Hanhowuz) the largest reservoir; irrigated area about 857,000 ha in 1975 and 1,744,100 ha in 1994, 37% saline; wheat and cotton the main crops

sources.title: Hanhowuz Reservoir, Turkmenistan
sources.note: The reservoir stores winter runoff and canal overflow for summer and feeds the Tejen oasis; the canal has starved the Aral Sea; earthen canals lose nearly half of the water; seepage visible along the canal

sources.title: World of Change: Shrinking Aral Sea
sources.note: Diversions of the Amu Darya and Syr Darya for irrigation from the 1960s; the sea a fraction of its 1960 extent by 2000; salty dust with agricultural chemicals from the dry lakebed, a public health hazard, degrading the soil

sources.title: A Soviet sea, killed by an obsession with “white gold”
sources.note: The Kara Kum canal the greatest diversion from the Amu Darya; its waters began to flow into the canal in 1956
